newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SCHOLAR PREPARES FOR "SPOOKY" RETURN HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCHOLAR PREPARES FOR "SPOOKY" RETURN HOME.

text.p: Former Tottenham chairman Irving Scholar admits there will be "something spooky" about his return to White Hart Lane on Saturday as part of a new consortium which took control of Nottingham Forest this week.
For Scholar is a man who claims to have had Tottenham's white-and-blue blood pumping through his veins since he was a schoolboy in the 1950s.
He is the man who plotted the takeover of club he loved in the early 1980s, a man who always won Tottenham trivia quizzes on journeys to away matches with his friends.
In many ways he started the revolution which has led to the stock market boom in soccer today. Under Scholar, Tottenham were the first club to have a stock market listing in 1983.

Scholar is also the man who by his own admission "loved Tottenham as much as anyone in my own family", but ultimately the man whose love, passion and dedication to the club almost brought it to its knees in the early 1990s.

Scholar's grand plans for Tottenham to diversify into a lesiure-based company collapsed with debts of around 20 million pounds ($32.6 million) and the only way the club survived was with Scholar leaving to be replaced by Alan Sugar.

That was in 1991 and when he walked out of Tottenham he walked away from soccer, returning to his tax-haven home in Monte Carlo and getting back to the world of property where he made the fortune which enabled him to complete the transformation from terrace schoolboy to club chairman.
"Its very ironic that I am going back to Tottenham for my first match," he said this week.

"The last match I was involved in was the 1991 Cup final when Tottenham beat Nottingham Forest and that my first match back will be at Tottenham is, I have to admit, a little bit spooky. It will be very strange being back at White Hart Lane, supporting the visitors."
Scholar's return to Tottenham follows Monday's takeover at Forest by a consortium led by property developer Nigel Wray, who won control of the club in a 19 million pounds takeover deal.

Scholar is part of that consortium and, while chairman and directors do not take centre stage on matchday, they do have a huge influence on proceedings. And the presence of new men like Scholar at the City Ground has already been felt, with Dave Bassett joining Forest on Thursday as general manager leaving his former club Crystal Palace stunned by his departure.

Bassett will also be among the new men of Forest at White Hart Lane, a ground where Forest have done exceptionally well in recent seasons, including last year where they won 1-0 in the league and knocked Tottenham out of the F.A. Cup on penalties in a fifth round replay. They have lost only once there in the last six years.

Both clubs go into the match desperate for points. Tottenham are, on current form, the worst team in the division with just one win from their last seven matches, while Forest are still deep in relegation trouble.

Forest are playing with more commitment and passion under caretaker player-manager Stuart Pearce but without a win in their last four games, which includes an F.A. Cup defeat at second division Chesterfield.

They will be without goalkeeper Mark Crossley, a hero of their penalty shoot-out win 11 months ago. He is suspended following his dismissal in the cup defeat at Chesterfield and misses his first match for more than three seasons. Northern Ireland international Tommy Wright deputises.
Pearce returns from his own two-match ban to strengthen the defence but midfielder Ian Woan starts a suspension.
England striker Teddy Sheringham, who made his comeback from injury for Spurs in Monday's 4-3 defeat at West Ham, could be out again with the ankle injury that kept him out for six matches.

But 2.6 million pounds defender John Scales finally looks set for his full Tottenham debut nine weeks after arriving from Liverpool and suffering a hamstring injury in only his second match as a substitute.

Spurs, who currently have the worst record in the division with only win in their last eight matches, are in no immediate danger of the drop in 11th place. But manager Gerry Francis admits: "We must start picking up points again or we'll be looking over our shoulders."

While Tottenham will be aiming to win to make sure they do not get embroiled in the relegation dogfight and Forest will be desperate for the points to help them climb away from danger, Manchester United look like consolidating their lead at the top of the table at home to Coventry.
Second-placed Liverpool play Aston Villa on Sunday, which will allow third-placed Newcastle to close the gap to two points if they beat strugglers Southampton at home.

Newcastle's England striker Alan Shearer will miss the match against his first club after undergoing groin surgery this week which could leave him sidelined for the rest of the season. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
